newsitem.title: USA: Dean Foods to buy Marie's salad dressing.
newsitem.headline: Dean Foods to buy Marie's salad dressing.

text.p: Dean Foods Co., maker of Birds Eye frozen vegetables as well as dairy products, said Wednesday it agreed to acquire the Marie's salad dressing business from Campbell Soup Co.
As part of the deal, Dean Foods will acquire a manufacturing plant and distribution centre in Thornton, Ill., which will add needed capacity to the company's existing operations, it said.
With sales of about $35 million, the Marie's line of refrigerated salad dressings, vegetable dips, salsas and fruit glazes is distributed throughout most regions of the country.

"With the leading national market share among refrigerated salad dressings, Marie's is well-positioned in the fast-growing produce section of the supermarket," said Howard Dean, chairman of Franklin Park, Ill.-based Dean Foods.
He added that the Marie's line of vegetable dips complements Dean Foods' Birds Eye dip line introduced two years ago.
"Marie's salsas have already achieved the No. 1 share among refrigerated salsas in only their second year of distribution," Dean said.
Dean Foods said Marie's business has an "excellent" broker organisation and a strong licensing arrangement for the manufacture and sale of products in nine western states.
The acquisition is expected to close within 30 days, subject to regulatory approval.

Dean Foods produces branded and private label fluid milk, cottage cheese and ice cream sold under the Dean's and other regional brand names. It also makes Freshlike and Veg-All as well as private label frozen vegetables. Dean Foods is also a leader in private label pickles and non-dairy coffee creamers.
Dean Foods' stock fell 25 cents to $39.375, while Campbell rose 25 cents to $50.25 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
